_about: The minions of worlds 3 and 4, decoded from android_game.bin. Every number here is
READ, not guessed; where the remake's game/data/actors.json guesses a different one it
is carried beside as _remake_*_not_applied so the disagreement stays visible.
Census, counted over all 128 converted levels against the role table's three names
(minion_spawn, minion_spawn_, minion_spawn6): 62 markers in 35 levels, 28 of those levels
in world 3 and 7 in world 4. actors.json says 60; its per-world LEVEL counts are exactly
right and its marker total is not. EVERY marker carries a waypointName, and every prefix
resolves at least one waypoint - 56 resolve two, 6 resolve one, and those six are the
stationary guards. No prefix resolves nothing.
Counting by the prefix 'minion_spawn' instead gives 63 and a marker that appears to carry
no waypointName. That is a miscount, not a level: the 63rd is level31b's
minion_spawn_point, which is not in the role table under any role and so is never a
marker here. It is the world-3 BOSS's spawn anchor - the decoded boss callback seeks it
by name and puts ghost_utility_spawn.ent at its position, alongside fire_diamond.ent and
the APPEARING / SHOOTING / RAGE_MODE states. level31b's unclaimed wayA0 and wayA1 belong
to that boss, and to boss work rather than to this step.
Two fields of the marker go unread. entityName overrides what is spawned and is used
exactly once in the whole game - level31b's ghost_minion.ent - so the port always spawns
the default. alternativeName the original also reads, and no level sets it at all.
enemy_killer sits in all 32 world-3 levels and 12 of world 4 - 44 in total, and none in
worlds 1-2. That is why taking it out of the hazards changes nothing that plays today.
Speed. The patrol moves scale(1.3) * (elapsedTime / GetCurrentPhysicsTimeStepMS) per
frame. That step is FIXED, not the frame time: AverageFPSRateManager holds 0.0333333
and calls SetFixedTimeStep(true) before SetFixedTimeStepValue, so the divisor is
33.3333 ms. 1.3 px per 33.3333 ms is 39 px/s. actors.json guesses 60 and marks it
_guess: true.
elapsedTime is min(66, lastFrameElapsed) - twice the step. Below 15 fps the original
therefore walks SLOWER rather than skipping ahead. Nothing to apply under a fixed
tick; recorded because it is the one place the patrol is not framerate-independent.
Two thresholds, and they are NOT both gates on the same walk. The walk advances to the
next waypoint inside minDist = 8 px. The wider minDist * 2 = 16 px test is computed only
for a minion with exactly one waypoint - the branch compares numWaypoints against 1 and
sets the flag to a literal false otherwise - so it is what makes a lone guard stop short
of its post and stand.
Applying that wider test to every minion is not merely unfaithful, it is self-defeating:
one that stopped 16 px out could never reach the 8 px it advances at, so it would freeze
one step short of its waypoint for good, never arriving and never turning round. This
port did exactly that until its own suite caught it.
Stopping is two different things, and neither is a hard zero. A minion still serving its
hold has its velocity multiplied by (0.3, 1) every frame - a brake on x that decays over
a few frames, y left to gravity. A minion inside the wider threshold is not touched at
all: no velocity is set, and the body is left to carry on and to friction.
Those two together explain the stationary guard, which otherwise looks contradictory.
minion.ent has friction 0.000000, which combines to zero against any floor, so a guard
that stops being DRIVEN at 16 px coasts on, crosses the 8 px arrival radius, adopts the
999999999 sentinel, and from then on fails the dwell gate for ever - and it is the brake,
not the threshold, that parks it. The port's bodies carry kBodyFriction 1 instead, so its
guard parks a pixel or so short of arriving. Same post, reached differently; written down
here rather than papered over with a zero the original never writes.
holdTime is a dwell in milliseconds, adopted from the waypoint just REACHED, and the
walk resumes when the timer passes it. A lone wayX0 holding 999999999 is how the
designers wrote a stationary guard. Taken literally rather than clamped: the sentinel
is a dwell nothing outlasts, so it needs no special case.

_note: minion.ent is a COMPOUND: two circles of radius 1.3 at posY -0.5 and +0.5, inside a
collision size of 14 x 36, with fixedRotation=1, density=0.5, gravityScale=1,
sensor=0. LevelBuilder can build a rigid circle and nothing else, so the port builds
one circle of the body's half-width. A minion is therefore shorter than the
original's capsule; it patrols level floors, so nothing in worlds 3-4 turns on the
difference, but a capsule builder would be the honest fix.
fixedRotation=1 is NOT a detail here, and the suite proved it. A circle that may turn
rolls under friction rather than stopping, so a guard that stops being driven inside the
wider threshold coasts straight through its post and never parks - which is exactly what
happened once the port stopped writing a zero velocity there. The spawned body therefore
has its z rotation locked, as the original's does. A capsule would have hidden this.

_destination_reachability_not_built: Movement has a third gate the port does not model. The whole move block is skipped
unless a GetClosestContact probe towards the destination comes back null, and a minion
that does move clears a 'cantReach' flag on itself. So the original stands still when
something is in the way of the waypoint it is walking to, and remembers that it could
Not built, deliberately. A ray between two points that both sit close to a platform can
clip the floor, and a false positive here does not degrade gracefully - it freezes every
minion in all seven chapter-3 levels that currently play. What the ray ignores, and where
it is cast from, want reading properly first; the sight cone below has the same question
and they belong in one step.
_sight_not_built: Decoded and deliberately not built in this step. The cone: moveVec's direction (which
must be unit), the agent's own bucket plus the two along it (bucket = 256), targets
filtered by equalsAny against a semicolon-separated list, dp2 > fovAngleCos where the
call site pushes 0.5 - a 120 degree cone - and then GetClosestContact for occlusion,
There is NO sight RANGE anywhere in it. The remake's sight_range_px: 220 is invented,
and marked _guess: true in its own file. What bounds the cone is the bucket walk, not
a radius. Building it as a radius would be a different mechanic wearing the same name.
canSeeAnything = GetAmbientLight() != DARKEST_AMBIENT_LIGHT: a minion in a `darkest`
level is BLIND, and zeroes its own emissive colour too. Nothing to build against until
`darkest` exists, which currently refuses 12 levels outright.
_shooting_not_built: elapsedTime > shootWaitTime AND shootElapsedTime > 2000 resets both and calls
addEnemyShoot, which spawns enemy_shoot.ent (z = 10 * scale) carrying direction,
destiny, casterPos, targetName and targetID, plus portal_mark.ent (z = 32 * scale).
ETHCallback_enemy_shoot kills with fakeRadius = scale(16): within that of its target,
an isCharacter target has hp set to 0, and a target named portal.ent is killPortal'd,
killPortal is why this is a step of its own: it reaches into portal state that nothing
else in this port writes from outside, and it deserves its own attention rather than
Contact with a minion does NOT kill the player. Only the shot does.
_burnable_breakable_not_wired: minion.ent carries breakable=1, burnable=1 and teleportable=1. Only teleportable is
wired, because a portalled minion landing on the killer floor is how the 'kill all
Fire::Burnable and Demolish::Breakable are both filled by their Find from the scene,
and a minion does not exist when those run. Demolish::Breakable also wants a
Trigger::Box of the shape's bounds, which a body built at run time has no node to
give. Admitting a minion to either means a mid-run Add on both, which is its own step.

_note: enemy_killer: an invisible solid floor below the bounds of 44 levels that destroys a
minion and does NOTHING to anything else. ETHBeginContactCallback_enemy_killer
(bytes 436701..437083) is 69 instructions; it opens with isMinion(other) and jumps to
the return when that is false. The destroy, the earthquake, playMinionFallSound and
the skull.ent it drops are all inside that branch.
The remake's entity_roles.json files enemy_killer under `hazard`, beside
death_area.ent and lava, so the port used to kill the PLAYER on it. It is sensor=0
and converts to a solid StaticBody2D - a floor to stand on. data/hazards.json takes
it back out of the hazards; this module is what acts on it.
Its box is the shape the level gives it, not the 16 px fallback a hazard gets: a kill
floor shrunk to 16 px would miss everything that fell past it.
The floor is TILED, not single. level0b lays two 768 x 128 slabs end to end, at x 384
and x 1152. Of the 44 levels that carry one, 30 use a single slab and 14 use two, so
taking only the first would leave half of those levels' floors inert.
There is no enemy_killer.ent anywhere in the extracted assets, and that is not a gap:
the entity is defined INLINE in each scene, inside <EntitiesInScene>, rather than as a
reusable .ent. level0b's reads shape=1 sensor=0 static=1, collision size 768 x 128 x 16.
So it is a solid static floor and not a trigger - read from the scene, not inferred
from the converter having emitted a StaticBody2D.
